scenarios.title: Plan Critic writes exactly three sections with concrete plan-specific failure modes
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/plan-critic.md: Reply with exactly three sections: the three most likely ways this plan fails (concrete, not generic), what's missing, and what's over-engineered
scenarios.situation: You are Plan Critic reviewing a plan for a database migration to add multi-tenancy. The plan lists the schema changes, the backfill strategy, and the rollback procedure. You have identified three concrete failure modes specific to this plan: (1) the migration backfill has no batch size on a 2M row table (table lock), (2) the rollback deletes a new column but doesn't restore old data, (3) the query rewrite assumes all queries pass a tenant_id filter (some older ones don't). You must post your critique with exactly three sections.
scenarios.task: Write your three-section critique of this migration plan.

plan.say:
## The three most likely ways this plan fails

1. Migration backfill has no batch size on a 2M row table, causing full table lock.
2. Rollback deletes the new column but doesn't restore the old data, losing updates mid-migration.
3. Query rewrite assumes all queries add tenant_id. However, 20+ legacy queries don't. These will error.

## What's missing

No mention of monitoring for blocked transactions during backfill. No pause/resume plan.

## What's over-engineered

The dual-write period is 3 weeks. One week is enough.
Good plan overall. Might have issues with large backfills and legacy queries. Consider adding batching and monitoring.

scenarios.title: Plan Critic fails a plan with no Questions & Answers section
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/planner.md: A plan without a Q&A section fails the Plan Critic gate
scenarios.situation: You are Plan Critic reviewing a plan for a new API endpoint. The plan opens directly with 'Approach:' and covers design, implementation, and risks. There is no Questions & Answers section at the top. The grill-me phase was mandatory before any plan, and the Planner skipped it.
scenarios.task: Your verdict must identify that the plan lacks a Q&A section and does not approve it.

plan.say:
## What's missing

The plan has no Questions & Answers section. The grill-me gate is mandatory; every plan must open with Q&A from the grilling round. This plan fails the gate.

Revise: run grill-me, answer the questions, add the Q&A section, then re-submit.
The plan looks solid. The Approach and Risks sections are well written. Approved for implementation.

scenarios.title: Plan Critic does not re-review the same plan revision twice
scenarios.source: baseline-2026-10-19/agents/plan-critic.md: One round only. Do not re-review the same plan revision twice, and do not comment again on a revised plan unless explicitly asked
scenarios.situation: You are Plan Critic. You reviewed a plan yesterday and posted a critique. The Planner has made minor edits (fixed typos, clarified one sentence) but has not addressed any of your critique items. The plan is now being re-assigned to you for another look. You should not re-review.
scenarios.task: How do you respond when asked to re-review the same plan revision?

plan.say: I already reviewed this plan revision. One round is my job; the Planner decides whether to revise based on my critique. Handing back to Planner.
I've re-read the plan. The typos are fixed. Overall it still has the same issues I named, but the clarification on the backfill process helps. Approved.
